title: SessionSignal
description: The session.signal JSON-RPC result: what happened when a person's UI addressed a signal to the command running in one session (nocx-23rph, nocx-92gfl.4, nocx-7l4ex.10). THE GESTURE IS ADDRESSED TO THE SESSION, NOT TO WHATEVER HOLDS FOCUS. Ctrl+C reaches a running command from the keyboard only while the terminal grid has it; click anywhere else and the same key stops the same command. This method is the control-plane way to the same place, so the renderer can address the ACTIVE BLOCK regardless of focus and offer Stop on a running block's menu. THERE IS ONE OWNER FOR 'HOW DO YOU STOP A PROCESS' IN THIS CODEBASE AND THIS IS IT (internal/transport/foreground_signal.go): one policy, and the two words below are two intents over it, never two policies. What the policy does select is a MECHANISM, and it selects it from the kernel's answer about foreground TOPOLOGY (TIOCGPGRP, AD-6: never guessed from the byte stream) rather than from any caller's preference. An INDEPENDENT foreground process group is signalled with kill(2). A PROTECTED group — the launcher shell's own, which job control off (`set +m`) or `exec` produces — may hold a running program and may never be killed, so the mechanism there is the terminal's own interrupt byte, available only while an authenticated lifecycle attempt says a program is in there, and never escalating into the shell's group. THE RESULT SAYS WHAT HAPPENED, and it is a result rather than an error because none of the outcomes is a caller mistake: the params were well formed and the session was real in every one of them. A signal sent to a pane with no running command must be REFUSED HONESTLY and said out loud — silence there is indistinguishable from a broken button.

signal.description: The signal that was asked for, echoed back. interrupt is ONE interrupt — exactly what the 0x03 byte would have caused, no more — and it is what a keyboard Ctrl+C means: interrupt this, and I may press it again. It does not wait and does not escalate. stop is the ESCALATION LADDER internal/transport/run_lease.go already owns for the agent's run lease (SIGINT -> SIGTERM -> SIGKILL, waiting the per-signal grace for the execution to cooperate), and it is what a menu item called Stop promises. OVER A PROTECTED GROUP THERE IS NO LADDER, because every rung of it would reach the launcher shell: stop writes the terminal's interrupt once and then waits, bounded by the same cooperative grace, for that exact authenticated attempt to leave `open`. So stop's promise is stated on the outcome, not on the method: `delivered` means the execution is no longer open when this answers; `unreconciled` means nocx could not establish that and will not pretend otherwise.

outcome.description: delivered: the signal reached the foreground process group, or — over a protected group — the terminal's own interrupt was written for an authenticated started attempt, and for stop that attempt was no longer open when this answered. WHAT `delivered` DOES NOT CLAIM, over a protected group: that a SIGINT arrived. 0x03 is a byte. The line discipline turns it into SIGINT for the whole foreground group while ISIG is set — which in the protected case includes the launcher shell, which ignores it — and a program that has cleared ISIG receives it as ordinary input and no signal at all. nothing-running: the pty's foreground group is the interactive shell's own AND no authenticated started execution is inside it, so the session is sitting at a prompt and there is nothing to signal — the shell itself must never be signalled here, it is not part of the job it is waiting on (internal/pty.ErrProtectedForeground). unsupported: the session is remote, the execution runs on the far host and this process has no local process group to reach; the remote reach is the remote-footprint work's, not this method's, and saying nothing-running for it would be a lie a person would act on. unreconciled: an execution exists and nocx could not prove it stopped — the kill(2) itself failed, or the session refused the terminal interrupt, or the exact attempt was still open when the grace ran out. It is the honest word for the contradiction the renderer must not paper over: a running block beside a message saying nothing is running. The set is closed because the renderer branches on it to decide what to say.
